title: DBM chief urges public to monitor public funds via 'COMPASS' spending tracking platform
summary: Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Secretary Kim Robert De Leon urged the public to use the government's unified budget transparency platform to monitor how public funds are released and…

blocks.text: Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Secretary Kim Robert De Leon urged the public to use the government's unified budget transparency platform to monitor how public funds are released and spent, and to ensure that the institutions managing them are held accountable.

In a news release on Saturday, the DBM, citing Episode 20 of A.S.K. – Alamin Kay Sec. Kim— said the Budget chief demonstrated how Filipinos can use the Centralized Open Monitoring Platform for Appropriations and Spending Statistics (COMPASS) to view available information regarding government funds, from budget allocation to actual expenditure.

In September, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Executive Order No. 126 on September 28, institutionalizing the Centralized Open Monitoring Platform for Appropriations and Spending Statistics (COMPASS).
The DBM said it aims to consolidate into a single online platform financial information that previously had to be searched for across various government institutions.

Under EO No. 126, concerned national government agencies and instrumentalities, including government-owned or -controlled corporations (GOCCs) and government financial institutions (GFIs), are mandated to submit, publish, and update the information required under the EO.
Local government units (LGUs) are also encouraged to participate.

Through the initiative, public access to information will be broadened, institutional accountability will be strengthened, and citizens will be encouraged to participate in monitoring the use of public resources, according to the DBM.

COMPASS will also be linked to existing digital systems, including the integrated Financial Management Information System, Budget and Treasury Management System, Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System, Digital Information for Monitoring and Evaluation, and the E-Gov PH App.
Meanwhile, the COMPASS Council will oversee the platform.

Malacañang said the council will be chaired by the DBM and co-chaired by the Department of Information and Communications Technology. The Department of Finance and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) will serve as members. —VAL, GMA News
